artists.biography: Split Enz were a New Zealand band of the 1970s and early 1980s featuring Phil Judd and brothers Tim Finn and Neil Finn. They achieved chart success in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada during the early 1980s’ most notably with the single "I Got You", and built a cult following elsewhere. Their musical style was eclectic and original, incorporating influences from art rock, vaudeville, swing, punk, rock, new wave, and pop.

They achieved chart success in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada during the early 1980s’ most notably with the single "I Got You", and built a cult following elsewhere. Their musical style was eclectic and original, incorporating influences from art rock, vaudeville, swing, punk, rock, new wave, and pop.

perplexity.description:
Mental Notes," released in July 1975, is the debut album by New Zealand rock band Split Enz. The album showcases a blend of rock with strong influences from art rock and progressive rock, characterized by complex arrangements, theatrical vocals, and a distinctive use of synthesizers and unconventional song structures. This style set the foundation for the band's evolving sound and distinguished them within the 1970s rock scene.

As the first major release in Split Enz's discography, "Mental Notes" captures the band's early experimental phase, reflecting their transition from their original name, Split Ends, to Split Enz. The album was released on Demon Records and is noted for its ambitious musicality and artistic presentation, including elaborate cover art. While not a major commercial success at the time, it received critical recognition for its originality and helped establish the band's cult following, paving the way for their later, more commercially successful works.
